label.en: Medical interpreting: clinical encounters and meaning

jurisdiction.region: General interpreter practice; specific legal/clinical rules labeled by source

label.en: Access, encounter structure and interpreter role

translationAreas.description: Important. Map referral, scheduling, intake, team introductions, handoffs and remote participation; distinguish interpreting from advocacy, explanation and clinical decision making within sourced standards. Evidence responsibility: a sourced encounter map and role-boundary cases including access barriers and communication repair. Sources: professional interpreter standards and health-system language-access guidance. Queries: 'healthcare interpreter standards role boundaries remote encounter'; 'hospital interpreter patient language access workflow'.

Critical. Cover presenting concern, history, allergies, prior care, family/social context, symptom chronology and examination speech. Evidence responsibility: source-grounded distinctions among reported symptom, observed sign, tentative explanation, differential consideration and established diagnosis; preserve attribution, uncertainty, negatives and time. Sources: public clinical encounter explanations and patient history materials. Queries: 'patient history physical examination symptoms signs diagnosis uncertainty patient information'; 'medical history allergy adverse reaction patient information'.

label.en: Functional anatomy, physiology and common conditions

translationAreas.description: Important. Build functional models for cardiovascular, respiratory, gastrointestinal/hepatobiliary, renal/urinary, endocrine/metabolic, neurologic, musculoskeletal, skin, sensory, hematologic/immune and infectious-disease encounters. Evidence responsibility: each system receives a relevant structure/function model, common consequential presentations and condition distinctions linked to actual encounter tasks; justify depth through frequency and consequence rather than encyclopedic disease lists. Sources: national health agencies and institutional patient education. Queries: '[body system] anatomy symptoms diagnosis treatment patient information'; '[condition] patient information complications follow-up'.

Critical. Cover specimens, laboratory tests, imaging, screening, diagnostic testing, preparation and result follow-up. Evidence responsibility: contextual distinctions among indication, preparation, procedure, finding, interpretation and next step; investigate positive/negative, normal/abnormal, screening/confirmation and uncertainty without inventing universal thresholds. Sources: public laboratory, imaging and screening explanations. Queries: 'medical tests understanding results reference ranges patient information'; 'imaging contrast preparation patient information'; 'screening diagnostic test false positive patient information'.

Critical. Cover medicine identity, purpose, formulation, route, strength, dose, frequency, duration, changes, missed-dose questions, allergies, adverse effects and reconciliation. Evidence responsibility: preserve quantity relationships, units, instructions and conditional wording; distinguish source-supported medication concepts without supplying treatment advice or unsupported conversions. Sources: official medicine labels, public medicines agencies and patient medication instructions. Queries: 'medicine patient information strength dose route frequency'; 'medication reconciliation patient information allergy side effects'; 'Spanish Chinese official medication patient information'.

Critical. Research common surgery, anesthesia, bedside procedures, devices, wound care, rehabilitation and supportive treatment according to encounter importance. Evidence responsibility: source-linked preparation–procedure–recovery models, participant roles, choices, restrictions and follow-up language; preserve conditional instructions and avoid implying universal protocols. Sources: hospital and professional-body patient materials. Queries: 'procedure anesthesia recovery patient information'; 'rehabilitation wound care device instructions patient education'.

Critical. Cover options, benefits, harms, alternatives, refusal, consent discussions, understanding checks and source-specific capacity arrangements. Evidence responsibility: preserve voluntariness, actor, uncertainty, probability framing and distinctions between permission, understanding and agreement. Label jurisdictional rules rather than presenting one consent model as universal. Sources: public consent policies, patient decision resources and interpreting standards. Queries: 'patient informed consent shared decision making risks alternatives'; '[jurisdiction] healthcare consent capacity interpreter official guidance'.

label.en: Pain, urgent assessment and emergency transitions

translationAreas.description: Critical. Cover pain quality/location/radiation/severity, injury, triage, acute deterioration, emergency procedures and rapid handoffs. Evidence responsibility: retain sequence, onset, attribution, severity wording and urgent instructions under interruption; distinguish emergency workflow language from interpreter-led clinical triage. Sources: emergency-care patient materials and professional interpreting guidance. Queries: 'emergency department triage assessment patient information'; 'pain description onset severity patient assessment'; 'emergency medical interpreting communication standards'.

label.en: Mental health, distress and substance-related encounters

translationAreas.description: Critical. Cover assessment, therapy, crisis conversations, substance use, withdrawal and safety-related language as supported by sources. Evidence responsibility: preserve speaker perspective, disfluency, idiom, reported experience, intent and uncertainty; investigate stigma, euphemism and interpreter role boundaries. Source every legal restriction or disclosure duty by jurisdiction. Sources: public mental-health services, patient resources and specialist interpreting standards. Queries: 'mental health interpreting assessment idiom interpreter guidance'; 'mental health crisis substance use patient information'; '[jurisdiction] mental health consent confidentiality official'.

Critical. Cover sexual history, reproductive anatomy, contraception, pregnancy, birth, postpartum care and pregnancy loss; investigate violence-related encounters and safeguarding boundaries through appropriate evidence. Evidence responsibility: accurate anatomical and patient-preferred language, chronology, privacy concerns, euphemism and sensitive clarification without assumptions about identity or family structure. Sources: authoritative sexual/reproductive patient education and jurisdiction-labeled safeguarding guidance. Queries: 'sexual reproductive health patient information interpreter'; 'pregnancy childbirth postpartum loss patient information'; '[jurisdiction] safeguarding healthcare interpreter guidance'.

label.en: Chronic care, life course and serious illness

translationAreas.description: Important. Cover recurring chronic-care visits, self-management discussions, prevention, pediatric/developmental encounters, older-person care, disability-related access and serious-illness/palliative conversations. Evidence responsibility: preserve goals, baseline/change, prognosis uncertainty, caregiver versus patient attribution and follow-up responsibilities; distinguish care concepts that lack institutional equivalents. Sources: public disease-management, pediatric, geriatric and palliative patient resources. Queries: 'chronic condition self management follow-up patient information'; 'pediatric older adult healthcare communication interpreter'; 'palliative goals of care prognosis patient information'.

Critical. Cover discharge instructions, medication changes, referrals, appointments, home care, return precautions and administrative access language. Evidence responsibility: complete source-grounded transitions identifying who must do what, when, where and under which condition, including unresolved results and failed communication. Sources: institutional discharge and referral materials. Queries: 'hospital discharge instructions medication follow-up pending results patient'; 'patient referral appointment preparation language access'.

label.en: Clinical register, quantities and document interpretation

translationAreas.description: Critical cross-cutting responsibility. Audit every chapter for abbreviations, names, numbers, units, dates, negation, probability, time, professional/patient register and supported Spanish/Chinese false friends or variants. Evidence responsibility: contextual bilingual dossiers and sight/remote document cases with ambiguity and clarification boundaries; no invented equivalents or decontextualized abbreviation expansions. Sources: originating clinical documents, authoritative multilingual patient materials and language references. Queries: '[clinical concept] official patient information español 中文'; '[abbreviation] [clinical context] official patient information'.
